extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in TikTok's policies, moderation, privacy, and controversies
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes TikTok/Douyin platform policies, content-moderation criteria, privacy/data practices, monetization eligibility, and related enforcement and transparency measures. Covers examples, exceptions, and implementation notes reported in media and studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal content prohibition categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal guidelines against the promotion of violence, separatism, and 'demonization of countries' could be used to prohibit content related to topics like the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre, Falun Gong, human rights in Tibet, Taiwan, Chechnya, Northern Ireland, the Cambodian genocide, the 1998 Indonesian riots, Kurdish nationalism, ethnic conflicts, and criticism of world leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are cited as potential grounds for censorship; critics say they are non‑transparent and can be applied broadly to suppress politically sensitive topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Douyin banned content list
rubrics_metrics.description: Douyin guidelines forbid live broadcasting by unregistered foreigners, 'feudal superstition', 'money worship', smoking and drinking, competitive eating by the 'already obese', 'toxic' slime, 'pornographic' ASMR (e.g., ear-licking), and female anchors wearing revealing clothes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are region-specific (China) platform rules replacing earlier global guidelines; presented as examples of localized/customized moderation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderator suppression criteria (appearance/poverty/disability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderators were instructed to suppress posts from 'For You' recommendations if the users shown were deemed 'too ugly, poor, or disabled'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as part of internal moderation instructions — cited as evidence of discriminatory suppression practices and a problematic moderation criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heating/manual promotion policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'heating' tool allows TikTok to manually promote certain videos (initially comprising 1–2% of daily views); used to grow and diversify content and influencers not picked up by the recommendation algorithm and to promote brands, artists, and NGOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports note abuse by employees promoting personal accounts, TikTok's statement that only a few individuals can approve heating in the US and promoted videos take up less than 0.002% of user feeds, and proposed safeguards (vetted US security personnel, third-party audits like Oracle) to address influence concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: STEM feed reliability and age-appropriateness checks
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok introduced a dedicated STEM feed that works with Common Sense Networks to check for safety and age appropriateness and with the Poynter Institute for reliability of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes third‑party partnerships used as content vetting criteria for a subject-specific feed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic content detection and blacklist
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok maintains a blacklist that detects graphic content before being uploaded; used to remove shocking or graphic videos (e.g., beheading video) and other graphic suicide content identified in recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited of viral graphic content detected and removed; blacklist is presented as an automated/preventative enforcement mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misinformation policy actions and election integrity measures
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok has banned Holocaust denial, added links to accurate COVID-19 information on tagged videos, removed misinformation videos (e.g., election and COVID-19 related), and created an in-app Elections Center in multiple languages, partnering with authorities like the National Association of Secretaries of State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites removal counts (e.g., hundreds of thousands of videos removed) and external evaluations (NewsGuard) comparing search-result quality to other platforms; also notes criticisms and limitations in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extremism and hate speech moderation
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok has removed accounts posting ISIL propaganda and execution videos and has policies against hate speech, but research and reports document instances where extremist and hateful content (e.g., Holocaust denial, neo-Nazi propaganda) circulated and were promoted by the algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses enforcement actions (account removals, search term blocks), ongoing spread via audio remixing and AI-generated content, and calls for tighter restrictions due to youth user base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creator Rewards monetization eligibility and revenue share
rubrics_metrics.description: Creators with a video reaching the top 4% of the platform and with more than 100,000 followers are eligible to receive 50% of its ad revenue under the Creator Rewards Program (which replaced the Creator Fund).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also notes prior monetization mechanisms (Creator Fund finite pool) and other tools like Creative Exchange that connect creators to sponsorship deals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influencer disclosure and advertising guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Influencers and creators are expected (or suggested) to disclose paid promotions; reporting highlights cases where influencers failed to disclose ads (e.g., FeetFinder campaigns) and platform/industry calls for transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of non-disclosure and platform responses (suggestions to be upfront about who funds content) show enforcement and ethical norms around influencer marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teenage mode and age-based restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok/ Douyin implement teenage modes and parental controls: default screen time limits for users under 18, under-13 users require a parental passcode to extend time, mandatory screen time limits for under-14 (in China), and requirements to link accounts to a real identity to prevent false ages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies are presented as responses to government pressure and safety concerns, with region-specific implementations and criticisms about adequacy and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underage user safety measures (messaging, livestreaming, content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific protections include forbidding direct messaging for users younger than 16, raising the minimum age for livestreaming from 16 to 18, removal of accounts failing age verification, and parental account management features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include mass removals in Italy for failing age checks, fines for inadequate protections, and cases of underage users exposing personal routines and risks from challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection disclosures in privacy policy
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok's privacy policy lists collected data types: usage information, IP addresses, mobile carrier, unique device identifiers, keystroke patterns, location data, inferred interests based on content viewed, and content created by users; it can also track non-users via web activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy is cited as broad and 'vague' by experts; studies (Citizen Lab) found collection within industry norms but concerns remain about extent and implications in jurisdictions with weak privacy laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biometric data potential collection
rubrics_metrics.description: In June 2021 TikTok updated its policy to include potential collection of biometric data, including 'faceprints and voiceprints', for special effects and other purposes; user authorization would be requested if local law demands such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts called the wording vague and potentially problematic for regions like the US lacking robust biometric protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data residency, access controls, and Project Texas
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Texas aims to silo privileged US user data within the United States under oversight (USDS) and third parties (e.g., Oracle) to address unauthorized access and state influence; measures include routing US traffic through Oracle Cloud, deletion of backups elsewhere, USDS management of user data/software/code/moderation under CFIUS oversight, Oracle spot-checks, digital signing of code, and localized physical review locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as TikTok's proposed technical and governance controls to reassure US regulators; reporting notes ongoing negotiations with CFIUS and critiques that some implementations may not go far enough.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Clover and European data localization plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Clover involves discussions with the UK's National Cyber Security Centre to store European user information locally, building data centers in Ireland and Norway and appointing a third party to oversee cybersecurity, data flows, and personnel access independently of TikTok.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as regional data-residency solution analogous to Project Texas to address European regulatory concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access and sharing with corporate group
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok can share data with its corporate group, including ByteDance; policy updates stated global corporate group employees from China and elsewhere could gain remote access to European user account information based on 'demonstrated need'; reports also indicated some US creator financial data were stored in China.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as the basis for concerns about potential Chinese government access; company statements and technical mitigations (Project Texas, routing through Oracle) are noted in response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency measures and third‑party review
rubrics_metrics.description: After scrutiny, TikTok said it would grant some outside experts access to anonymized data sets and protocols, including filters, keywords, criteria for heating, and source code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as partial transparency efforts; outside researchers and watchdogs have critiqued the sufficiency and methodology of disclosed datasets and studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement metrics and takedown reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok publishes or reports removal/enforcement statistics: counts of removed fake accounts, fake followers, impersonating accounts, videos violating civic integrity, prevented fake likes/follow requests, dismantled coordinated networks, and numbers of videos removed for misinformation or policy violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as evidence of enforcement activity in specific episodes (e.g., Moldovan election interference, Russian propaganda); also cited in debates about transparency and comparability to other platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political content and fundraising restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok banned fundraising for political accounts (noted in 2022) and created election-centre features to provide accurate local election information; it also removed state media accounts (e.g., RT, Sputnik) in some regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures are described as attempts to protect civic integrity but have been accompanied by disputes about content moderation fairness and national-security-driven actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and Creative Center limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok restricted the number of hashtags that can be searched under its Creative Center after claims of 'misuse to draw inaccurate conclusions'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as a change to reduce external scraping/analysis leading to misleading inferences; cited as an example of restricting data access that affects researchers and journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff misuse and nepotism safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports indicate some employees abused heating to promote their own accounts or those of spouses, prompting statements that only a few individuals can approve heating and discussions of vetting/auditing (e.g., CFIUS oversight, Oracle auditing) to reduce abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as implementation concern and rationale for further oversight and limited approval privileges.
